title: The goal and the rules of the game
blurb: What the team wants this model to become, and the rules it set for itself so that its results can be trusted.

scenes.heading: The goal: think first, then talk

caption.text: The model should think first and talk second.
It should learn from a few examples.
It should beat models of its whole size.
One day, it should beat Minecraft like a person.

scenes.heading: The size bar: gain more from size

caption.text: The team's rule: with more numbers, our design must gain more than a plain model does.
A plain model is a standard model of the same whole size, practised the same way.
The check climbs a ladder of sizes.
Not shown yet for the finished design: earlier runs had a bug, so they do not count.

scenes.heading: Inside: learned. Outside: hand code

caption.text: The team's rule: everything inside the model is learned.
Hand-written code may run only as a tool the model chooses to call, like the calculator.
A deployed model must do its own learning, sleeping (night study), stopping and picking.
Not finished: some hand-written steps are still on the answer path.

scenes.heading: Rules so the practice stays honest

caption.text: No practice answer is ever cut short.
Pass marks are written down before a run.
Questions kept aside for the exam are never practised on.
No new teacher: only the 171,940 teaching rows we have, plus human-written web text.
A win claim needs 6 or more paired copies. A 2-copy screen only decides whether to try.

scenes.heading: The spend rule: one big proven run

caption.text: The team's rule: spend big only on a run that demonstrably works, not on many small tests.
So it climbs a size ladder on the project's own PC and Macs. No rented machines now.
The 100 million run waits for the Oct 31 readout, planned.
Estimate for that run: 3 to 6 weeks on the PC alone.

scenes.heading: How sure is the team? Not 90% yet

The plan's own judgement, not measured: about 1 in 3 that the design out-scales a plain model.
For the Minecraft goal: well under 1 in 10.

scenes.heading: The scorecard: nine goals, none green yet

caption.text: The plan keeps a scorecard of nine goals, each with a pass mark written in advance.
Part-way shown: skills, its own thinking, running itself, honest practice, creativity, new domains.
Red: hand-written parts still sit on the answer path. Untested: bigger helps more, and beating its whole size.
Today, none of the nine is fully green.
